answer: Each identity posts a bond whose key lives in a hardware root, so one machine cannot quietly back a hundred accounts. Submissions carry a fresh nonce, and a repeated nonce freezes the bond instead of paying it. Payouts leave as a vesting stream across many epochs. A farm must own real devices, keep every nonce unique, and wait out vesting before taking anything. The trade-off is explicit: payouts pulse slowly for honest agents too, and the zenith of a farm is capped by the devices it can bond while a prism of mirrored accounts stays expensive to hold.
